name: Psyllium
summary: Psyllium is the soluble fiber from the husks of Plantago ovata seeds, best known as a bulk-forming laxative. Because it forms a viscous gel that binds bile acids, it also affects blood lipids: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found that psyllium supplementation lowered LDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B versus control, with roughly 10 grams per day a commonly studied dose. Psyllium should be taken with ample water and separated in time from other medications, whose absorption its gel can slow.
description: Psyllium is not a classic phytochemical-heavy herb; its value comes from gel-forming husk fiber. That makes it more of a functional-fiber tool than a general botanical tonic.
safetyNotes: Must be taken with plenty of water; choking or bowel obstruction risk in dysphagia/strictures. Separate from oral medications by 2-4 hours.
interactions: Potential interaction concern with antidiabetic medicines
use clinician review for high-dose extracts or chronic use.
